backlog.title: CLI Subcommand Resolution & Config Validation Bug Fixes
backlog.description: Fix three bugs identified in end-to-end testing of the §9.8 (repo-root), §9.7 (.hack config), and §5.3 (breakdown-in-progress) delta: (1) BUG-001 Critical — 6 of 7 subcommands resolve plan/ & PRD.md against the invocation dir instead of the repo root because action handlers run during program.parse() before main()'s chdir; (2) BUG-002 Minor — .hack validation/secrets errors render with a full stack trace via the default catch arm instead of the clean single-message arms used for typed errors; (3) BUG-003 Minor — the documented commit.retry_delay_cap_ms >= commit.retry_delay_ms relational constraint is not enforced. All fixes use existing infrastructure (Commander preAction hooks, typed-error pattern, per-key validation framework). No new dependencies.

milestones.title: BUG-001: Fix subcommand repo-root resolution (Critical)
milestones.description: Fix the root cause where 6 of 7 subcommands (task, status, cache, inspect, artifacts, validate-state) resolve plan/ and PRD.md against INVOCATION_CWD instead of the repo root. Only the `config` subcommand was patched (src/cli/index.ts:608). The fix uses a Commander preAction hook (supported in commander@14.0.2) to resolve the repo root + chdir before ANY action handler runs, making all subcommands inherit correct cwd with a single-point change. See architecture/bug_001_fix_strategy.md for the detailed design.

tasks.title: PreAction hook for repo-root bootstrap
tasks.description: Create a shared bootstrapRepoRoot() helper and register a Commander preAction hook that resolves the repo root + chdirs before any action handler runs. Update main() to consume the already-bootstrapped singleton instead of re-resolving. Simplify the config handler to remove its now-redundant inline resolveRepositoryRoot call.

subtasks.title: Create bootstrapRepoRoot() helper in src/utils/repo-root.ts
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/009_94353b1a9fd3/bugfix/001_412283d974f7/architecture/bug_001_fix_strategy.md for the full design. The existing resolveRepositoryRoot() at src/utils/repo-root.ts:147-160 resolves the repo root and sets singletons _repoRoot/_invocationCwd. getRepoRoot() (line 170) reads _repoRoot (throws if unset). getInvocationCwd() (line 182) reads _invocationCwd. There is currently no chdir encapsulation — main() does resolveRepositoryRoot() then process.chdir() as two separate steps (src/index.ts:147-150).
2. INPUT: A startDir string (typically process.cwd() === INVOCATION_CWD at hook time) and optional opts object { explicit?: string } (for --repo-root override).
3. LOGIC: Implement an exported `bootstrapRepoRoot(startDir: string, opts?: ResolveRepoOpts): string` function in src/utils/repo-root.ts. It must: (a) check an idempotency flag (_bootstrapped); if true, return getRepoRoot() immediately (prevents double chdir if Commander fires the hook for both program and subcommand levels); (b) call resolveRepositoryRoot(startDir, opts) (which sets the singletons and throws NotARepositoryError if no .git); (c) call process.chdir(repoRoot); (d) set _bootstrapped = true; (e) return repoRoot. Also export a `_resetBootstrap()` function (test-only, resets _bootstrapped to false) for unit test setup/teardown. Import the existing ResolveRepoOpts type from the same file. Do NOT modify resolveRepositoryRoot itself — bootstrapRepoRoot wraps it.
4. OUTPUT: Exports `bootstrapRepoRoot` and `_resetBootstrap` from src/utils/repo-root.ts for consumption by P1.M1.T1.S2 (the preAction hook) and tests.
5. DOCS: none — no user-facing/config/API surface change. This is an internal helper.

subtasks.title: Wire preAction hook into parseCLIArgs() and update main() to use singleton
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/009_94353b1a9fd3/bugfix/001_412283d974f7/architecture/bug_001_fix_strategy.md and architecture/system_context.md. parseCLIArgs() is at src/cli/index.ts:274. program.parse(process.argv) is at line 853. All subcommand .action() handlers (inspect@485, artifacts@510, validate-state@540, cache@569, config@599, taskAction@625) execute INSIDE program.parse(), BEFORE main()'s chdir at src/index.ts:150. Commander v14.0.2 supports program.hook('preAction', listener) where listener receives (thisCommand, actionCommand) — see architecture/external_deps.md. The hook fires AFTER options are parsed (program.opts() has --repo-root) but BEFORE the action body. If the hook throws (e.g. NotARepositoryError), the error propagates through program.parse() to parseCLIArgs() to main() to main().catch() which has a dedicated NotARepositoryError clean arm (src/index.ts:417-420) — desired behavior.
2. INPUT: bootstrapRepoRoot() from P1.M1.T1.S1. The existing program object in parseCLIArgs(). The --repo-root option registered via program.option('--repo-root <path>'...).
3. LOGIC: (a) In src/cli/index.ts, add `import { bootstrapRepoRoot } from '../utils/repo-root.js';` (resolveRepositoryRoot is already imported at line 44 — add bootstrapRepoRoot to that import). (b) Before program.parse(process.argv) (line 853), register: `program.hook('preAction', () => { const opts = program.opts() as { repoRoot?: string }; bootstrapRepoRoot(process.cwd(), opts.repoRoot ? { explicit: opts.repoRoot } : undefined); });`. The process.cwd() call here is correct — at hook time no chdir has run yet, so cwd === INVOCATION_CWD. (c) In src/index.ts, replace lines 147-150 (the resolveRepositoryRoot + process.chdir) with: `const repoRoot = getRepoRoot();` — the preAction hook already bootstrapped during program.parse() for the default path too. Add `import { getRepoRoot } from './utils/repo-root.js';` to src/index.ts (or extend the existing repo-root import). Keep the bootstrap comment but update it to explain the hook. (d) Ensure src/index.ts still has INVOCATION_CWD available for the --prd pre-resolution logic (it should be unaffected — INVOCATION_CWD is captured at module load, line 55).
4. OUTPUT: All action handlers (including subcommands task/status/cache/inspect/artifacts/validate-state) now see process.cwd() === repoRoot when their bodies execute. NotARepositoryError from the hook propagates to main().catch()'s dedicated clean arm. main() consumes the singleton via getRepoRoot().
5. DOCS: none — the behavior change brings the implementation into alignment with existing PRD §9.8.7/§9.8.9 acceptance criteria. No docs describe the broken behavior.

subtasks.title: Simplify config handler — remove redundant resolveRepositoryRoot inline call
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See architecture/bug_001_fix_strategy.md Step 4. The config action handler (src/cli/index.ts:599-621) currently calls resolveRepositoryRoot(process.cwd(), ...) at line 608 INSIDE its try block, then passes repoRoot to ConfigCommand. After P1.M1.T1.S2's preAction hook, the hook already bootstrapped resolveRepositoryRoot + chdir before the config action handler runs. So the inline call is redundant and its process.cwd() would resolve against repoRoot (not INVOCATION_CWD) — harmless but misleading. The handler also has a comment block (lines 602-606) explaining why it resolves the repo root itself — this comment becomes stale and should be updated/removed.
2. INPUT: getRepoRoot() from src/utils/repo-root.ts (singleton set by the preAction hook from P1.M1.T1.S2).
3. LOGIC: In src/cli/index.ts config action handler (line 599-621): (a) Replace the inline resolveRepositoryRoot call + explicit extraction (lines 604-612) with `const repoRoot = getRepoRoot();`. (b) Remove the stale comment about subcommand dispatch running before the bootstrap chdir. (c) Add `getRepoRoot` to the import from '../utils/repo-root.js' (line 44). (d) The catch block (lines 617-621) can remain as-is — after the hook fix, NotARepositoryError no longer reaches this catch (it's thrown in the hook before the try block). Any other errors (from ConfigCommand.execute) still render via logger().error().
4. OUTPUT: Config handler uses the preAction-hook-bootstrapped singleton. No redundant resolveRepositoryRoot call. The stale comment is removed.
5. DOCS: none — internal refactor, no user-facing change.

tasks.title: Integration tests — subcommand resolution from subdirectories
tasks.description: Add integration tests that verify all 6 previously-unpatched subcommands resolve plan/ and PRD.md at the repo root when invoked from a nested subdirectory, and that NotARepositoryError renders cleanly when invoked outside any git repository. The current test suite tests the resolver in isolation and missed the action-handler timing gap.

subtasks.title: Integration tests: subcommands from nested subdir + outside repo
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See architecture/system_context.md §1 and architecture/external_deps.md for test patterns. Existing integration tests in tests/integration/repo-root-acceptance.test.ts use a subprocess pattern: `const tsxBin = resolve(process.cwd(), 'node_modules', '.bin', 'tsx'); const absIndex = resolve(process.cwd(), 'src/index.ts'); const runCli = (args, cwd) => spawnSync(tsxBin, [absIndex, ...args], { cwd, encoding: 'utf8' });`. Git repo fixtures use `makeRepo()` which does `mkdtempSync` + `git init -q`. The §9.8.9 acceptance criteria require: (a) launched from nested subdir → resolves plan/PRD.md at repo root; (b) outside any repo → exit 1 with clean ❌ message. The §5.3 breakdown-in-progress notice must also work from a subdir (hack status from src/deep/nested during in-progress breakdown → calm notice, not 'No sessions found').
2. INPUT: The preAction-hook-based fix from P1.M1.T1.S2 (all subcommands now resolve against repo root). The spawnSync test helper pattern from tests/integration/repo-root-acceptance.test.ts.
3. LOGIC: Create a new integration test file (e.g., tests/integration/cli/subcommand-repo-root.test.ts). Test cases: (a) For each of the 6 subcommands (task, status, cache, inspect, artifacts, validate-state): create a real git repo tmpdir with plan/NNN_hash/tasks.json + PRD.md at the root; create a nested subdir (src/deep/nested); run the subcommand from the nested subdir via spawnSync; assert exit code and that it resolves paths at the repo root (not the subdir). (b) For NotARepositoryError: create a non-git tmpdir; run `hack task` and `hack validate-state` from it; assert exit 1 + stderr contains 'No .git entry found' or '--repo-root' remediation + NO stack trace. (c) For §5.3 synergy: create a git repo with a session dir that exists but has no tasks.json; run `hack status` from a nested subdir; assert it prints the calm breakdown-in-progress notice (not 'No sessions found'). Use afterEach/beforeEach to clean up tmpdirs and restore process.cwd(). Call `_resetBootstrap()` if importing parseCLIArgs directly, but for subprocess tests this is not needed (each spawnSync is a fresh process).
4. OUTPUT: A test file that proves the §9.8.7/§9.8.9 acceptance criteria pass for ALL subcommands when invoked from a subdirectory, closing the integration-test gap that allowed BUG-001 to ship.
5. DOCS: none — test-only.

milestones.title: BUG-002: Clean error rendering for config validation errors (Minor)
milestones.description: Introduce a typed HackConfigError class for .hack validation failures (BOM, parse, secrets, type/range/enum) and add a dedicated clean catch arm to main().catch() so these user-facing misconfigurations render as a single actionable ❌ line without a stack trace, consistent with the existing NotARepositoryError/AuthPreflightError arms. Also add an EnvironmentValidationError arm (same gap). See architecture/bug_002_fix_strategy.md.

tasks.title: Typed HackConfigError class and throw-site conversion

subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:

Existing classes: NotARepositoryError (src/utils/repo-root.ts:65), AuthPreflightError (src/config/types.ts:219), HarnessProviderMismatchError (src/config/types.ts:175), UnsupportedHarnessError (src/config/types.ts:142), EnvironmentValidationError (src/config/types.ts:79). The 9 throw sites in src/config/hack-config.ts are: line 83 (BOM in parseHackFile), line 90 (TOML parse in parseHackFile), line 774 (secrets policy in validateHackTier), lines 815/820/826/832/837/847 (type/range/enum in validateFieldValue). The validateFieldValue doc comment (hack-config.ts:799-803) explicitly says 'A plain throw new Error reaches main().catch()'s default arm (index.ts:401) → exit 1.' — update this to reference HackConfigError + the new clean arm.
2. INPUT: The existing src/config/types.ts typed-error class patterns as templates.
3. LOGIC: (a) In src/config/types.ts, add: `export class HackConfigError extends Error { constructor(message: string) { super(message); this.name = 'HackConfigError'; } }`. (b) In src/config/hack-config.ts, add `import { HackConfigError } from './types.js';`. (c) Replace all 9 `throw new Error(...)` with `throw new HackConfigError(...)` — keep the message strings IDENTICAL (they are already correct and actionable). The 9 sites are at lines 83, 90, 774, 815, 820, 826, 832, 837, 847. (d) Update the validateFieldValue JSDoc (lines 799-803) to say 'A throw of HackConfigError reaches main().catch()'s dedicated HackConfigError arm → clean ❌ message + exit 1.' instead of referencing the default arm.
4. OUTPUT: All .hack validation errors are now typed HackConfigError. Messages are unchanged. Downstream catch arms can use `instanceof HackConfigError` for clean rendering (consumed by P1.M2.T2.S1). The hack config validate CLI path (config.ts:489-528) uses `e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e)` which works identically (HackConfigError extends Error, same .message).
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Update the JSDoc comment on validateFieldValue (src/config/hack-config.ts:799-803) to reflect that throws are now HackConfigError reaching a dedicated clean arm. This rides WITH the work.

tasks.title: Clean catch arms in main() and tests
tasks.description: Add HackConfigError and EnvironmentValidationError clean arms to main().catch() so these user-facing errors render as a single ❌ line without a stack trace. Add tests verifying the clean rendering.

subtasks.title: Add HackConfigError + EnvironmentValidationError clean arms to main().catch()
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See architecture/bug_002_fix_strategy.md. main().catch() is at src/index.ts:404-423. It has 4 dedicated clean arms (AuthPreflightError@405, HarnessProviderMismatchError@409, UnsupportedHarnessError@413, NotARepositoryError@417) each rendering `console.error(\`\n❌ ${error.message}\`); process.exit(1);`. The default arm (line 421) renders `console.error('\n❌ Fatal error in main():', error); process.exit(1);` which dumps the full Error object with stack trace. EnvironmentValidationError (src/config/types.ts:79) also lacks a dedicated arm and hits the default. Import environmentValidationError/HackConfigError classes into src/index.ts — note src/index.ts already imports from './config/types.js' (check existing imports). P1.M1.T1.S2 dependency is because that subtask also modifies src/index.ts (main's bootstrap section); ensure the catch-arm changes are in the .catch() block and don't conflict with the getRepoRoot() change in the main body.
2. INPUT: HackConfigError class from P1.M2.T1.S1. EnvironmentValidationError class from src/config/types.ts:79. The existing clean-arm pattern from main().catch().
3. LOGIC: In src/index.ts main().catch() (lines 404-423), insert BEFORE the default arm (line 421): `if (error instanceof HackConfigError) { console.error(\`\n❌ ${error.message}\`); process.exit(1); }` and `if (error instanceof EnvironmentValidationError) { console.error(\`\n❌ ${error.message}\`); process.exit(1); }`. Ensure HackConfigError is imported (from './config/types.js') and EnvironmentValidationError is imported (it may already be — check src/index.ts imports). The placement order among the clean arms does not matter (each exits on match).
4. OUTPUT: .hack validation errors (BOM, type/range/enum, secrets, parse) and environment validation errors now render as a single `\n❌ <message>` line + exit 1, without a stack trace. Consistent with NotARepositoryError/AuthPreflightError rendering.

subtasks.title: Tests: verify clean rendering (no stack trace) for config validation errors
subtasks.context_scope:

subtasks.title: Implement commit relational check + remove gap comments + tests
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See architecture/bug_003_fix_strategy.md. validateHackTier is at src/config/hack-config.ts:755-805. It loops over sections → keys and calls validateFieldValue per key (type/range/enum). After the loop, there is NO post-validation cross-key check. The HACK_CONFIG_SCHEMA commit section (hack-config.ts:617-625) has retry_delay_ms { type:'int', min:0 } and retry_delay_cap_ms { type:'int', min:0 }. The HackConfigFieldSpec interface (hack-config.ts:587-594) has no relational metadata field. The two gap comments are at hack-config.ts:602-603 (JSDoc on HACK_CONFIG_SCHEMA) and hack-config.ts:625 (inline on retry_delay_cap_ms field spec). Both runtime paths call validateHackTier: hack config validate CLI (config.ts:507 calls validateHackTier per file) and loadHackConfig startup (hack-config.ts:952 calls validateHackTier per tier). P1.M2.T1.S1 dependency: use HackConfigError for the throw (if P1.M2 not yet done, plain Error works — same message).
2. INPUT: The validateHackTier function (src/config/hack-config.ts:755-805). The parsed config object (ParsedHackConfig) which has a `commit` section with keys retry_delay_ms and retry_delay_cap_ms (if authored). HackConfigError from P1.M2.T1.S1.
3. LOGIC: At the END of validateHackTier (after the `for (const [section, keys] of Object.entries(parsed))` loop), add: `const commit = parsed.commit; if (commit && commit.retry_delay_ms !== undefined && commit.retry_delay_cap_ms !== undefined) { const delay = commit.retry_delay_ms as number; const cap = commit.retry_delay_cap_ms as number; if (cap < delay) { throw new HackConfigError(\`[commit] retry_delay_cap_ms in ${file}: ${cap} is less than retry_delay_ms (${delay}); the cap must be ≥ the base delay.\`); } }`. Use HackConfigError (imported in P1.M2.T1.S1). Remove/update the gap comment at hack-config.ts:602-603 (JSDoc on HACK_CONFIG_SCHEMA — remove the 'DOCUMENTED GAP' sentence). Update the inline comment at hack-config.ts:625 from '// relational cap>=delay deferred (cross-key)' to '// relational cap>=delay enforced in validateHackTier'. Add unit tests in tests/unit/config/hack-config.test.ts: (a) cap < delay (e.g. retry_delay_ms=200000, retry_delay_cap_ms=100) → throws with message containing 'retry_delay_cap_ms' and 'less than'; (b) cap >= delay (e.g. retry_delay_ms=1000, retry_delay_cap_ms=10000) → passes (existing test at line 895-919 already covers the pass case — ensure it still passes); (c) only one key present → passes (no relational check fires).
4. OUTPUT: validateHackTier enforces the §9.7.5 relational constraint. Both hack config validate and real startup reject cap < delay configs. The gap comments are removed. Tests prove the rejection and the pass case.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Update the JSDoc on HACK_CONFIG_SCHEMA (hack-config.ts:602-603) to remove the DOCUMENTED GAP note (the check is now enforced). Update the inline comment on retry_delay_cap_ms (hack-config.ts:625). These ride WITH the work.
